chapter: Funerals, dances and the end of the parades
title: Crossing Canal Street, no trouble uptown, and the good old music times
summary: White says nobody gave him trouble across town, Allen remembers the Young Tuxedo, and White says the old club members have died out.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: You'd go across Canal Street and everything?
Well, would the guys uptown ever give you a hard time?
Mm-mm. None. I mean mostly all of them. I'll be weep around West we go. All around West we go. I'mma tell you the truth, most all them boys know of me. Every one of them. White like black.
You know I used to follow the young tuxedo up around West we go and I don't see them up there anymore. I just thought of them.
You know why? Most of them all mostly all, if they, some of them, if they ain't dead they must be awake.
Yeah, I guess those old members of the clubs die out.

More, more, yeah. You see like, in them time they used to, them time, them time they would, they didn't have no, them time they used to be good time for music. You used to pay someone money for music. I know I want to pay enough for music. I don't know I want to pay enough for music. I don't know where I'm so much so long.
